title: Rent adjustment/credit for tenant-paid maintenance or repairs
description: Tenants sometimes pay out-of-pocket for plumbing, repairs, or maintenance and ask the warden to deduct that amount from their rent instead of reimbursing in cash. There is currently no way to record this - a warden either has to manually shrink the invoice amount (losing the paper trail of why) or track it outside the app. Resolved design question: this needs a real credit/adjustment entity (its own table, FK'd to tenant + optionally an invoice), not a manual override of Invoice.amountDue - an override would silently disconnect the invoice from LODGY-16/22's 'every number traces to a real record' invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: A new Credit/Adjustment entity exists (amount, reason/note, tenant, optional linked invoice, createdAt) - not a mutation of the invoice's own amountDue field
Warden can record a maintenance/repair credit against a specific tenant with an amount and a short note
The credit is applied to reduce that tenant's next (or a chosen) invoice's effective amount due, and is visible on the invoice as a labeled line item, not just a smaller total
Credit history is visible on the tenant's notes/timeline
Reports (Monthly Report, CSV export) reflect the adjusted amounts by summing invoice + credit rows, not by reading a pre-adjusted cached total

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.
Resolved the data-model question: build a real Credit/Adjustment table rather than overriding amountDue directly.

Starting - a real Credit table (not a mutation of Invoice.amountDue), a Room migration 1 -> 2, effective-due arithmetic that every consumer of an invoice total goes through, and the credit surfaced as its own labelled line rather than a quietly smaller number.

Credits are a real table, not an invoice mutation. New Credit entity (id, tenantId, nullable invoiceId, amount, reason, createdAt/updatedAt) with FKs to tenants (CASCADE) and invoices (SET NULL), plus CreditDao/CreditRepository. DB went to version 2 with a hand-written MIGRATION_1_2 - v1 is on a real warden's phone, so this migrates rather than wipes; the migration SQL was diffed against Room's own exported schemas/2.json and matches it exactly, indices included. Invoice.amountDue is never touched: all the arithmetic goes through one function, data/InvoiceTotals.kt effectiveAmountDue(), which also caps relief at the invoice total so a credit cannot push an invoice negative into a refund the app has no way to hand back. Every consumer routes through it - the invoice list total, the record-payment prefill AND the UNPAID/PARTIAL/PAID recalculation (a credited invoice paid down to its reduced balance now correctly reads PAID rather than sticking at PARTIAL), the reminder message's amount, and the Monthly Report. The credit shows as its own labelled 'Credit: ₹x' line on the invoice row and on the payment screen next to an 'after credit' figure - a labelled line item, not a quietly smaller number. Monthly Report gained a Credits tile and a Credits row in the CSV, computed by summing invoice and credit rows at read time with nothing pre-adjusted cached anywhere. Recording is More-free: a 'Record a credit' action on the tenant profile opens CreditFormScreen (amount, reason, and a target of either a specific unsettled invoice or 'Next invoice'); choosing 'Next invoice' stores invoiceId null and InvoiceGenerationWorker attaches everything still pending to the invoice it generates, so the applied state is explicit data rather than an implicit rule. The tenant timeline now merges notes and credits into one date-sorted list (TimelineEntry sealed interface), credits read-only there. Tests: InvoiceTotalsTest for the arithmetic including the over-credit cap, CreditFormViewModelTest for target selection and validation, RecordPaymentViewModelTest for the reduced prefill and the PAID transition, MonthlyReportViewModelTest for dues/credits summed from rows and scoped to the period, NotesTimelineViewModelTest for interleaving. testDebugUnitTest green.

FAIL on AC2 - the credit feature is well built but unreachable on a default-density phone. AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 all pass. AC1: there is a real credits table (id, tenantId, invoiceId, amount, reason, createdAt) and the invoice's own amountDue is NOT mutated - after an 800 credit the invoice row still reads amountDue 3000.0. AC3: the invoice list shows 'Credit: 800' as a labelled line with the effective 2200 beneath it, and the receipt PDF renders 'Invoice amount 3000 / Credit applied 800 / Amount due 2200' as separate lines rather than one silently shrunken total. AC4: the timeline shows 'Credit 800 - Plumbing repair'. AC5: reports sum invoice + credit rows - the Monthly Report for 5/2026 shows Total collected 2200, Credits 800, Total dues 0, and the CSV export carries a distinct "Credits","800.00" row. THE PROBLEM: AC2 says the warden can record a credit against a tenant. The 'Record a credit' card sits on the tenant profile below the fold, and that screen does not scroll - at the emulator's stock 1080x2400 @ 420dpi the profile is clipped after 'Pay several months at once' and swiping does nothing. Same single root cause as LODGY-34: TenantProfileScreen.kt:88, root Column has no verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()). I only reached the credit form by dropping the display to 280dpi. This should clear as soon as that one modifier is added - no changes needed to the credit feature itself.

Fixed by the same one-line change as LODGY-34 - no changes to the credit feature, which QA had already passed on AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5. TenantProfileScreen's root Column now scrolls, so 'Record a credit' is reachable at stock 420dpi. VERIFIED ON EMULATOR at default density: the card is reachable by scrolling on an ACTIVE tenant's profile. Build and full suite green: 412 tests pass (4 new), ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug both successful. Tests touched for the new signatures: TenantProfileViewModelTest and TenantDirectoryViewModelTest now mock the observed agreement flows, InvoiceListViewModelTest gains the ReconciliationRepository mock, and DataPacketTest gains the noticeGiven label. Note on two profile tests: they assert state after setPlannedMoveOut, which previously passed only because the ViewModel wrote the value optimistically. Rather than keep that second source of truth - the exact bug class LODGY-33 is about - the mocks now use a MutableStateFlow that re-emits on write, which is how Room actually behaves.

PASS. AC2, the criterion this previously failed on, is met: 'Record a credit' is reachable on an ACTIVE tenant's profile at stock 420dpi now that the screen scrolls. AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 were already verified in the previous round and I spot-checked that the developer's changes did not disturb them - the credits table is still separate with the invoice's own amountDue unmutated, the invoice list still shows 'Credit: ₹800' as a labelled line above the reduced effective total, the timeline still shows the credit entry, and the Monthly Report still reports Credits as its own figure alongside Total collected. Worth noting for the record that this ticket and LODGY-34 were both fixed by the same single modifier on TenantProfileScreen's root Column, and the same change also restores Checkout, which had regressed against the already-delivered LODGY-14.
